blocks.content: Quiz: Which of the following methods can be used to test how different browsers render your HTML page?
Tap an option below to answer:
The W3C Validator only checks your code against web standards and catches syntax errors. It does not show how the code renders on different browsers.
The W3C Validator only checks your code against web standards and catches syntax errors. It does not show how the code renders on different browsers.
Open the HTML page in each browser and look for differences.
By opening your HTML page in different browsers, you can check how it renders and behaves in each of these environments.
By opening your HTML page in different browsers, you can check how it renders and behaves in each of these environments.
Upload the file to the website server and check online.
Uploading to a server helps to make the webpage available online but doesn't necessarily guarantee consistency in rendering across different browsers.
Uploading to a server helps to make the webpage available online but doesn't necessarily guarantee consistency in rendering across different browsers.
Use Google Chrome only since it's the most popular.
Although Google Chrome is widely used, relying only on one browser for validation may lead to inconsistencies on other browsers.
